item.title: 60 Bhartṛyajña
item.description:
[[P551]]

  1. Bhartryajña

This seems to have been a very ancient commentator. Medhātithi1 in his bhāṣya on Manu 8. 3 says ‘other explanations have been well brought out by Bhartryajña and they should be understood from his work’. Trikāṇḍa-maṇḍana ( who flourished before 1100 A. D. ) in his Āpastambasūtra-dhvanitārtha-kārikā2 ( I. 41 ) refers to the views of Bhartryajña that one who had committed to memory the text of the Veda had the privilege ( the adhikāra ) of consecrating the sacred fires, though he may be innocent of the meaning of the Vedic texts. From Ananta’s bhāṣya it appears that Bhartryajña composed a bhāṣya on the Kātyāyanaśrautasūtra which had been lost ( utsanna ) in the former’s day. From Gadādhara’s comments on the Pāraskaragṛhyasūtra it appears that Bhartryajña commented on Pāraskara.3 The Gṛhastharatnākara of Caṇḍeśvara quotes Bhartryajña’s explanation of

item.title: 61 Viśvarūpa
item.description:
[[P553]]

  1. Viśvarūpa

The commentary of [[Viśvarūpia|Viśvarūpa]] called Bālakrīḍā on the [[Yājsavalkya-smrti|Yājñavalkya-smṛti]] has been recently published in two parts by M. M. T. Gaṇapati Śāstri in the Trivandrum Sanskrit Series. The Mit. states in the introductory verses that the dicta of [[Yij.|Yāj.]] were expanded by the voluminous or ample ([[vikata |vikaṭa]]) explanations of [[Viśvarūsra|Viśvarūpa]]. In commenting on Yāj. I. 81 the Mit. tells us that [[Viśvarūjia|Viśvarūpa]] looked upon the words of Yāj. I. 79 ([[tasmin yugmāsu saṁviset|tasmin yugmāsu saṃviśet]]) as a niyama. In Viśvarūpa’s commentary on Yāj. I. 80 ([[evam gacchan|evaṃ gacchan]] &c.) we do find that the verse of Yāj. and similar passages of Manu (3. 45), Vasiṣṭha and Gautama (5. 1) are understood to contain a [[niyam|niyama]] and not a [[prescinkhyu.?!!|parisaṅkhyā]]1 On Yāj. III. 24 the [[Mit, inforins|Mit. informs]] us that Viśvarūpa, Medhātithi and [[Dhāre svara|Dhāreśvara]] looked upon certain texts of [[Rsyasriiga|Ṛṣyaśṛṅga]] on [[āściucu|āśauca]] as in conflict with well-known [[sinitis|smṛtis]] and discarded them. Mr. S. Sitaram [[Sūstri|Śāstri]] published (in 1900 at Madras) the text and translation of [[Viśvarūpia’s|Viśvarūpa’s]] comment [[ou|on]] inheritance and Mr. Setlur also published the [[wavahūrco|vyavahāra]] section. In the following pages the Trivandrum edition is relied on.

item.title: 62 Bhāruci
item.description:
1. Bhāruci

The Mit. on [[Yij.|Yāj.]] ( I. 81 ) says that [[Bhiruci|Bhāruci]] like [[Viśvaripa|Viśvarūpa]] held the view that the rule ‘[[rulertau bhūryam|ṛtau bhāryām]] gacchet’ was a [[niyanma|niyama]] and not a [[paristkrinkhayti|parisaṃkhyā]]. On [[Yij.|Yāj.]] II 124 the Mit. says that the explanation of ‘the fourth share’ to be given to [[un married|unmarried]] sisters [[oflered|offered]] by [[Asahiya|Asahāya]] and [[Medhitithi|Medhātithi]] was the

[[P566]]

proper one and not that of Bhāruci. The Parāśaramādhavīya1 and the Sarasvatīvilāsa ( para 133 ) inform us that Bhāruci was of opinion that unmarried sisters were only entitled to a provision for their marriage and were not entitled to a fourth share.

item.title: 63 Śrīkara
item.description:
1. Śrīkara

The Mit. on Yāj. II. 135 alludes to the view of [[Srikara|Śrīkara]] and others that the widow [[succeeded is|succeeded as]] heir to her deceased husband’s estate if it was small.1 The [[Smytisāra|Smṛtisāra]]2 of Harinātha attributes the same view to [[Srikara|Śrīkara]] and [[disappro ves|disapproves]] of it. On Yāj. II. 169 the Mit.3 cites the view of [[Srikara|Śrīkara]] about that topic and disapproves of it. Viśvarūpa also gives two explanations of that verse of Yāj., the first of which agrees with that of the [[Mit,|Mit.]] and the second is akin to [[Srikara|Śrīkara]]’s.

item.title: 64 Medhātithi
item.description:
1. Medhātithi

Medhātithi is the author of an extensive and erudite commentary ( [[bhusyu|bhāṣya]] ) on the Manusmṛti.

It is the oldest extant commentary on that smṛti. The bhāṣya of Medhātithi was first published about forty years ago by Rao Saheb V. N. Mandlik in Bombay and recently Mr. J. R. Gharpure of Bombay brought out an edition of Medhātithi which closely follows Mandlik’s edition. A critical edition of the bhāṣya based upon all the available [[Msg.|Mss.]] is a great [[clesideratum|desideratum]]. A new edition in two volumes based on several mss. edited by M. M. Dr. Ganganath Jha was published in the G. O. I. Series in 1932 and 1939. In this edition also ten verses in the 3rd adhyāya are wanting and in adhyāya nine there
